seoTitle: How to Set Up a Gumroad Account and Store
metaDescription: Set up a Gumroad account, sign in with Facebook, Google, X, Stripe, or email, and get your storefront ready. Includes exactly what Gumroad charges per sale.
intro: Starting to sell digital products on Gumroad begins with a single account screen, but which sign-in method you pick and how you fill out your profile afterward shapes how professional your storefront looks from day one. This guide walks through Gumroad's sign-up screen, the options it offers, and what to do once you're logged in and looking at an empty store for the first time.
costNote: Creating a Gumroad account and storefront costs nothing upfront. Gumroad instead takes a cut of each sale: 10% + $0.50 on a sale made through your own profile or a direct link, and 30% on a sale a customer discovers through Gumroad's own marketplace. There's no monthly subscription fee either way.

steps.heading: Look at what you're signing up for
steps.body: Before creating an account, look at Gumroad's own pitch: the homepage headline reads "Go from 0 to $1," with copy about starting with what you know and getting paid, next to a black Start selling button and a marketplace search bar. It's a low-friction pitch by design. Gumroad wants the signup itself to feel as easy as the promise, and the account creation screen you'll hit next backs that up.

image.caption: Gumroad's homepage pitch, "Go from 0 to $1," with the Start selling button that leads into account creation.

steps.heading: Create your account
steps.body: Clicking through to sign up lands you on a single screen with five ways in: continue with Facebook, continue with Google, continue with X, continue with Stripe, or use an email and password directly. Using Facebook, Google, X, or Stripe skips typing a password, and connecting through Stripe specifically can speed up payout setup later, since Stripe is one of the payment processors Gumroad supports. If you'd prefer to keep your creator account separate from other logins, the email and password fields below the social options work like a normal signup form. There's also a "Sign up" link in the top corner if you land on the login version of this screen instead.

image.caption: Gumroad's account screen, with Facebook, Google, X, and Stripe sign-in buttons above a standard email-and-password option.

steps.heading: Land on your dashboard for the first time
steps.body: Once you're authenticated, Gumroad drops you into your dashboard, which starts empty apart from a getting-started checklist. This is normal. There's no product, no sales, and no followers yet, so don't expect a polished storefront on the first screen. Treat this as your control room going forward: the left-hand navigation is where you'll create products, check sales, and adjust settings, so click through each section once before you start building.

steps.heading: Fill in your profile so your store isn't blank
steps.body: Before publishing anything, open your profile settings and add a name, bio, and profile photo. This is what a customer sees before they trust you enough to buy. A generic or missing profile is one of the fastest ways to make an otherwise solid product page look unfinished. Keep the bio short and specific about what you make; vague descriptions read as less credible than a plain sentence about the actual products you sell.

steps.heading: Add branding to your storefront
steps.body: Beyond the profile basics, Gumroad lets you customize colors and layout elements on your public store page so it doesn't look identical to every other creator's default setup. Consistent branding between your storefront, your product thumbnails, and any social accounts you link makes the whole operation look more established, which matters more than people expect for a first-time buyer deciding whether to trust a small, unfamiliar creator with their payment details.

steps.heading: Configure payment settings before you publish
steps.body: The last step before you're truly ready to sell is payouts. Depending on which sign-in method you used, Gumroad may already have a head start on this if you connected through Stripe, but you'll still need to confirm payout details in your account settings so earnings reach a bank account. Do this before your first product goes live, not after the first sale comes in. Chasing payout setup while a customer is waiting on their download is a worse experience for everyone involved.

faq.question: Is it free to create a Gumroad account and store?
faq.answer: Yes. Creating an account and setting up your storefront costs nothing upfront. Gumroad instead takes a cut of each sale: 10% + $0.50 on sales through your own profile or link, and 30% on sales made through Gumroad's marketplace.

faq.question: What sign-in options does Gumroad offer?
faq.answer: Continue with Facebook, Google, X, or Stripe, or sign up with a plain email and password. All five options sit on the same account screen.

faq.question: Do I need a business entity to sell on Gumroad?
faq.answer: No. Individual creators can sell on Gumroad without a registered business, though payout requirements may vary by country.

faq.question: Why is my dashboard empty after I sign up?
faq.answer: A brand-new account has no products, sales, or followers yet, so the dashboard starts with a getting-started checklist instead of live data. That's expected.

faq.question: Can I customize how my storefront looks?
faq.answer: Yes. You can add a profile photo, bio, and branding elements so your storefront doesn't look like a bare default template to visitors.
